PEF Fabrication and Characterization Preparation of Uniaxially Electrospun Fibers Based on the previous literature reports detailing preparation of PEF, solutions were created to replicate the fabrication procedures. Armstrong et al. prepared the original electrospun fibers by creating a solution of 0.2 g Matrimid and 0.2 g PEO in 10 mL of dichloromethane and electrospinning them at a flow rate of 0.070 mL/min, voltage of 28 kV, and a collector distance of 32 cm.22 Once electrospun, the fibers maintained a structure and diameter similar to those reported in the article as seen in Figure 19, demonstrating that the fibers could be successfully replicated. Figure 19. SEM images of uniaxially electrospun fibers composed of 1:1 Matrimid/PEO. Preparation of Coaxially Electrospun Fibers Fabrication of the co-axial based fibers was carried out. Based on previous results and success of electrospinning of Matrimid and PEO based fibers, these fibers were used as the shell in co- axial electrospinning. The core solution consisted of 0.3 g PEO mixed with 0.3 g SBA-15 in 10 mL DI water. The deposition was carried out on aluminum sheets. Flow rate of core solution was varied to increase the silica loading in the composite fibers. Initially both solutions were spun at 26 0.07 mL/min, which resulted in a theoretical silica loading of 60wt% in the electrospun fibers. After further testing, the flow rate of the core increased to 0.1 mL/min, while still maintaining the desired structure, increasing the theoretical silica loading to 68wt%. Figure 20 shows the SEM images of the unwashed fibers maintaining the desired structure. Since the theoretical silica loading in the fibers is just based on the SBA-15, the coated sorbent will weigh more while occupying the same volume, leading to loadings >75wt% if successful. Figure 20. SEM images of coaxially electrospun fibers with a shell composed of Matrimid/PEO and a core composed of SBA-15/PEO. Preparation of Core-Shell Porous Electrospun Fibers Once prepared, the electrospun fibers are not porous by default and they must be further processed to generate the pores. Armstrong et al. mentions washing the electrospun fibers in methanol in order to extract the PEO, opening transport pathways to the pores of the adsorbent material.22 Since there was no mention of the duration of washing, the timing of the wash was varied. Figure 21a shows the fibers displayed in Figure 20 that were washed for 24 h while Figure 21b shows the same fibers washed for only 5 min. In both cases, the desired fiber structure was still retained. Figure 21. SEM images of core-shell electrospun fibers washed by methanol for 24 h (left) and methanol for 5 min (right).
